clue.text: Mammal is eating fruit that's hidden on plant

indicators.note: a creature eating something has it inside, so one piece goes within the mammal's letters

parts.note: a cat is a mammal

indicators.note: the word on is tucked out of sight, so those letters vanish from the fruit

parts.note: a lemon is a citrus fruit
taken as written, then removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that some animal keeps devouring the concealed fruit on their plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' looks like a hidden-word signal, but here 'that's hidden' makes the little word vanish from the fruit rather than conceal the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing garden shrub, a kind of plant.

clue.text: One carpet, under a pound or free

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is under comes below, so the pound's letter sits on top

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra)
the Roman numeral for one is I
to carpet someone is to scold them, to berate them

explanation.surface: Someone weighs whether a cheap rug, under a pound, might as well be given away free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is the verb, to reprimand, not the floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: To free captives is to release them, to set them at liberty.

clue.text: Religious host keeps on with wine

indicators.note: the host keeps the other pieces held inside it

parts.note: an MC, master of ceremonies, hosts an event
taken as written
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A pious host who keeps going on about the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Monastic life is that of monks, a devout, religious way of living.

clue.text: Duck given meal on lake

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A duck is given a meal beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater species of duck.

clue.text: Butterfly rumoured to encircle Norse god

indicators.note: the word for rumoured goes all the way round the god's name

parts.note: something rumoured is said, as in 'it is said that'
Tyr is the Norse god of war

explanation.surface: A butterfly is said to circle around a figure from Norse myth.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyr is the one-handed war god of Norse myth, a frequent crossword visitor; 'to encircle' asks for the rumour word to go round him.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrids are a family of brown butterflies such as the meadow brown.

clue.text: Perhaps Fijian animal seen moving about

indicators.note: the letters of the two words shift around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone from Fiji, perhaps, reports a creature seen roaming around.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiji lies in Melanesia, so a Fijian is one example of a Pacific islander from that region.

clue.text: Nice pals brought round bunches of flowers

indicators.note: the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Friendly pals turned up carrying bouquets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like an adjective (or the French city) but its letters are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A panicle is a branching cluster of flowers, as on lilac or oats.

clue.text: Lethargic party type succeeded by new worker

indicators.note: what comes next follows on, so the other pieces come after

parts.note: a stag party is a kind of party, a pre-wedding night out for men
the ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A sluggish partygoer is replaced by a fresh employee.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is the British name for a bachelor party.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant means inactive or sluggish, like still water that does not flow.

clue.text: Transgressing president has little right to sound off

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president
R is the short form of right
to rant is to sound off loudly

explanation.surface: A president who breaks the rules has little right to complain loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant behaviour departs from the norm, straying beyond accepted limits.

clue.text: More than enough cake eaten by a boy getting fat ultimately

indicators.note: the cake is swallowed, ending up inside the other letters

parts.note: Dan is a boy's name
a bun is a small cake

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word fat

explanation.surface: A lad who scoffs too much cake ends up getting fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant means plentiful, existing in greater quantity than needed.

clue.text: Sort of racehorse to show desire, about fifty to one, little good

indicators.note: the word for desiring goes around the numerals

parts.note: to yearn is to long for something
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A gambler craving a horse at fifty to one odds, with little chance of it being any good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifty to one' looks like betting odds but gives Roman L and I; 'about' places LI inside YEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is a horse in its second year, the age at which racehorses are sold.

clue.text: Foul birds at sea after spillage

indicators.note: after being spilt, the letters land in a different order

explanation.surface: Seabirds are soiled after an oil spill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' is a verb here: to corrupt or debase.
explanation.definitionFit: To bastardise something is to corrupt or debase it, to spoil its purity.

clue.text: Hard bed at such a price is heavily reduced

definitions.text: at such a price is heavily reduced

parts.note: rock is hard
the bottom of a sea or river is its bed

explanation.surface: An uncomfortable bed offered at a cut-down price.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer by a property: goods offered at a price like this are steeply discounted.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock-bottom price is the lowest possible, so what sells at it has been cut drastically.

clue.text: Joy not certain in prayer

indicators.note: not means the word for certain is taken away

parts.note: joy is pleasure
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Joy is not guaranteed by praying.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest appeal or request, much as a prayer is.

clue.text: Bird brings bill round in bite

indicators.note: the bill and round go in the middle of the word for bite

parts.note: a peck is a small bite
AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A bird brings its beak round to take a bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' suggests a beak but is AC, account.
explanation.definitionFit: The peacock is the male peafowl, a large bird with a showy tail.

clue.text: The old man with upper-class leaning out to appeal to plebs

parts.note: pop is a word for father, the old man
a list is a tilt or lean, as of a ship

explanation.surface: Dad, a posh sort with leanings, tries to court the common people.
explanation.definitionFit: A populist politician seeks the support of ordinary people.

clue.text: When rattled, I react by showing bitterness

indicators.note: rattled means shaken up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone admits that when flustered they respond with sourness.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbity is sharpness or sourness of tone or taste.

clue.text: Male group embracing independent attitudes and values

indicators.note: the outer letters embrace the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A men's group takes on a maverick with new attitudes and values.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a fixed outlook, a person's habitual way of thinking.

clue.text: Girl holding demonstration will provide political initiative

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the protest inside it

parts.note: Dee is a girl's name
a march is a protest demonstration

explanation.surface: A girl staging a protest is starting a political move.
explanation.definitionFit: A demarche is a diplomatic step or political move, often a formal protest.

clue.text: Religious recluses glimpse heavenwards when accepting given task

indicators.note: the outer word accepts the other piece inside it
in a down answer, going heavenwards means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to glimpse is to see
a remit is an assigned task or brief

explanation.surface: Hermits catch sight of heaven when they take on their appointed duty.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'heavenwards' means read from bottom to top; 'accepting' means the reversed word takes the task inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eremites are hermits, people who live alone for religious reasons.

clue.text: Grabs bill to get expenses added

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
costs are expenses

explanation.surface: Someone snatches the bill so they can add their expenses on.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and confront them, sometimes seizing them.

clue.text: Audible support for member of the lords

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar or column

explanation.surface: Vocal backing is given to a member of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is the upper chamber of the UK Parliament, whose members are peers.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a noble entitled to sit in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Has-been is stunned when sponsor comes round

indicators.note: the sponsor's word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a backer is a sponsor
numb means stunned, without feeling

explanation.surface: A fading star is left dazed when a sponsor finally turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: A back number is someone out of date or no longer important, like an old magazine issue.

clue.text: Buried in messy litter, book — old text

indicators.note: the book's letter is buried within the mixed letters
messy means the letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: An old book's text is found buried under a heap of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' mixes LITTER to LIRETT; 'Buried in' puts B inside that, giving LIBRETT, then O.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the written words of an opera or musical.

clue.text: Section of orchestra lacking right part of score

indicators.note: lacking means the abbreviation is missing from the section's name

parts.note: the brass is the section of trumpets, horns and trombones

explanation.surface: An orchestral section is missing a key part of the score.
explanation.definitionFit: The bass line is the lowest musical part in a written arrangement.

clue.text: Poverty to leave a mark on big town

parts.note: to scar is to leave a mark
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Poverty leaves its mark on a large town.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcity is a shortage or lack, and poverty can mean a dearth of something.

clue.text: Attack group wanting a fight

parts.note: a set is a group
a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: A gang spoiling for a fight goes on the offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: To set about someone is to assail them physically or verbally.

clue.text: Writer endlessly gripping us — feature of exciting fiction?

indicators.note: the cut-down name grips the other word inside it
endlessly means the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Edmund Spenser, the Elizabethan poet of The Faerie Queene

explanation.surface: An author whose work holds us endlessly in its grip, as thrillers should.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the poet's final letter, and 'gripping' then holds the little word inside; 'gripping' doubles as a word for thrilling fiction in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the tension and anticipation that keeps a reader of thrillers turning pages.
